answer: Deploying an onyx root-of-trust hardware module prevents arbitrary agent cloning by tethering digital identity to physical silicon sealed inside velvet tamper-evident packaging. An attacker attempting a sybil cascade must acquire thousands of expensive physical microchips, incurring prohibitive capital costs that break the economic viability of mass identity spoofing. However, this cold-chain hardware binding fails if compromised upstream during transit to the jetty distribution hub, where rogue actors could intercept and flash unauthorized keys before deployment.
